newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-DEBUTANT NGOBE GIVES SOUTH AFRICAN VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEBUTANT NGOBE GIVES SOUTH AFRICAN VICTORY.

text.p: Debutant Dumisa Ngobe struck a long range shot to give South Africa a 1-0 win over Kenya at the start of the Four Nations Cup on Saturday.
South Africa share the lead at the top of the table with Australia, who earlier beat Ghana 2-0 at the King's Park rugby stadium.
Ngobe, one of five new caps for the African champions, blasted home a brilliant effort as South Africa made a rampant start to the match in front of 46 000-strong crowd.
But the South Africans faded after that and had to survive some anxious moments at the end as Kenya slowly forced their way back into the match.
South African captain Neil Tovey made a vital clearance off the line in the last minute from Henry Motego's shot as Kenya laid siege to the home team's goal.
In the first game, Australia were too strong and disciplined for a make-shift Ghanaian team who fielded just one of their regular internationals.
Damian Mori slipped his marker to head from close range just before half-time and Paul Trimboli added a second goal in the 69th minute after a quick counter-attack.
Trimboli was set in the clear by hard-working midfielder Craig Foster to score with a first-time shot.
Australia and South Africa meet next in the week-long tournament in Johannesburg on Wednesday, preceded by a clash between Ghana and Kenya.
The tournament serves as a warm-up ahead of the African zone World Cup qualifiers which kick off in November.
